chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of his companions (I think it was Muhammad ibn Ismail), who said:

One of us mentioned meat in the presence of Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), so he said: 'What meat is more delicious than the meat of the goat?' He said, 'So Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) looked at him and said: 'Had Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created a morsel that is more delicious than the lamb, it would have been sacrificed for Ismail (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: Why is lamb meat considered superior to goat meat in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) distinguishes between sensory preference and spiritual merit by noting that while goat meat is tastier, the lamb was chosen for the sacrifice of Prophet Ismail (peace be upon him), thereby elevating its status. This hadith illustrates the Shia scholarly principle that divine selection often transcends worldly aesthetics, linking the physical attribute of the lamb to its role in a pivotal prophetic event. The narration serves as a reminder that the value of creation is often defined by its utility in worship rather than its inherent physical qualities.
